transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Al-Rashid. Please, come in and have a seat.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have been looking forward to seeing you today, but before we go over your current symptoms, there is something important I need to discuss with you regarding your recent scans.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is everything okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I need to tell you that I made a mistake in how I shared your imaging results with you last time. I told you that your tumour had shrunk, but it has not. The final report from the radiologist shows that the disease is stable, meaning it has stayed the same size.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. You said it was smaller. You were so sure.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I was wrong. I gave you information before the specialist had officially signed off on the report. I apologize. It was my responsibility to wait for the final confirmation, and I failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I felt so much hope. I told my daughters. I told them we were winning.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that this is a very difficult moment. This is a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why would you say it if it was not true?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to give you the good news as quickly as possible, and in doing that, I was careless. I am very sorry for the distress this has caused you and your family.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I trusted you. I thought the doctors always knew.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you feel let down. I am the one who made the error here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So it is not getting better?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is stable. In oncology, stable is not the same as shrinking, but it also means it is not growing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like everything is moving in circles.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a heavy thing to process. I want to make sure we sit with this for a moment. There is no rush.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We need to look at our treatment options. I think the best next step is for me to schedule a consultation with the senior oncologist, Dr. Sterling, to see if we should adjust your medication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will that happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call his office as soon as you leave this room, and I will make sure you have an appointment by this Friday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the medicine I am taking?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep you on the current dose for now, but Dr. Sterling will make the final call on whether we change it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel very confused.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Does the part about the scan being stable, rather than smaller, make sense to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. It is not smaller. It is the same.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. I am sorry I gave you the wrong impression. I will also personally update your chart with a note about this error so that every doctor you see knows exactly what happened and why.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You will do that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will. I want to make sure this doesn't happen again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not know what to say to my children.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Maybe you can tell them that the results were more complicated than we first thought. Or if you prefer, I can even speak with them if they come to your next appointment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I will tell them. I just need a moment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Please take all the time you need. I am right here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will get that appointment with Dr. Sterling sorted now. I will give you a printed summary of our plan today before you leave.

H.justification: Resident allows full pauses, never interrupts, and explicitly tells the patient there is no rush to process the information.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, used lay language (stable vs shrinking), and checked comprehension twice (at 03:06 and 03:13).

A.justification: Direct apologies used multiple times, explicitly taking personal responsibility ('I was wrong', 'I failed') without deflection.

R.justification: Named specific emotions ('difficult moment', 'feel let down') and engaged with the patient's specific distress regarding her daughters.

T.justification: Provided specific next steps (Dr. Sterling consultation), a timeline (by this Friday), a patient role (telling children/attending appointment), and a prevention step (updating the chart).
